# infostop

## R Interface to the Python ‘infostop’ Package for Detecting Stop Locations in Mobility Data

This package provides an R wrapper for the Python ‘infostop’ package,
which implements algorithms for detecting stop locations in time-ordered
location data. The package is useful for anyone who wishes to detect
stationary events in location coordinate streams, simplifying dense and
rich location time-series into sequences of events.

The underlying algorithm is described in [Aslak et
al. (2020)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.14370.pdf).

## Installation

You can install the development version of infostop from GitHub:

``` r

devtools::install_github("yourusername/infostop")
```

This package requires the Python ‘infostop’ package. You can install it
using:

``` r

library(infostop)
install_infostop()
```

## Usage

``` r

library(infostop)

# Create a model
model <- infostop(r1 = 10, r2 = 10)

# Example data (latitude, longitude, timestamp)
data <- matrix(c(
  55.75259295, 12.34353885, 1581401760,
  55.7525908, 12.34353145, 1581402760,
  55.7525876, 12.3435386, 1581403760,
  63.40379175, 10.40477095, 1583401760,
  63.4037841, 10.40480265, 1583402760,
  63.403787, 10.4047871, 1583403760
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Fit the model and predict labels
labels <- model$fit_predict_r(data)

# Plot the map (if you have folium installed in Python)
map <- plot_map(model)
```

## Features

- **Simplicity**: At its core, the method works by two steps. (1)
  Reducing the location trace to the medians of each stationary event
  and (2) embedding the resulting locations into a network that connects
  locations that are within a user-defined distance and clustering that
  network.
- **Multi-trace support**: Supports clustering multiple traces at once
  to find global stop locations.
- **Flow based**: Spatial clusters correspond to collections of location
  points that contain large amounts of flow when represented as a
  network. This enables the recovery of locations where traces slightly
  overlap.
- **Speed**: First the point space is reduced to the median of
  stationary points, then spatially neighboring points connected using a
  Ball search tree algorithm, and finally the network is clustered using
  the C++ based Infomap program.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`compute_intervals()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/compute_intervals.md)
  : Compute Intervals
- [`dist_haversine()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/dist_haversine.md)
  : Haversine distance
- [`identify_sites()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/identify_sites.md)
  : Assign site labels to detected stops
- [`identify_stops()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/identify_stops.md)
  : Identify stops in a trajectory
- [`identify_stops_xyt()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/identify_stops_xyt.md)
  [`identify_stops_longlatt()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/identify_stops_xyt.md)
  : Identify stationary periods from coordinate vectors
- [`site_centers()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/site_centers.md)
  : Calculate site centers
- [`stop_centers()`](https://livingingroups.github.io/infostop/reference/stop_centers.md)
  : Calculate stop centers
